title: Eternal Life
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Eternal life is the gift of knowing God through Jesus Christ and sharing everlasting life with Him. It begins now in union with Christ and will be fully enjoyed in resurrection glory and God’s eternal kingdom.
summary: Eternal life is the gift of knowing God through Jesus Christ and sharing everlasting life with Him. It begins now in union with Christ and will be fully enjoyed in resurrection glory and God’s eternal kingdom.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is eternal life given to sinners. He grants life to all who believe in Him, keeps them by His power, and brings them into everlasting fellowship with the Father.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Eternal life is more than endless existence. Scripture defines it as knowing the only true God and Jesus Christ whom He has sent.

This life is a gift, not a wage. Sin earns death, but God gives eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.

Eternal life begins now for those who believe, because they are joined to Christ and have passed from death to life. Yet its fullness awaits resurrection and the completed kingdom of God.

The final vision of eternal life is life with God: no curse, the river of life, the face of God, worship, service, and reign with Him forever.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
People often think of eternal life only as going somewhere after death, but Scripture presents it as life with God through Christ. It is relationship, rescue, inheritance, and future glory.

This doctrine strengthens hope without reducing salvation to escape from hell alone. Christ saves sinners into everlasting communion with God.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Receive eternal life as God’s gift in Christ and live now as one who belongs to the age to come. Let knowing God become your highest joy, and let eternal life reshape your priorities, worship, endurance, and witness.
